title: dfo-docs roadmap track
description: One roadmap track, published at the path roadmap.json gives for it, such as roadmap/data.json. Holds that track's own category vocabulary and every entry in it, upcoming and released. Each track is authored and reviewed by the team that owns it, and a track publishes even when another track's document fails to build. Generate types from this schema rather than from an example. Votes are live, per-viewer state that changes without a rebuild, so they live in the site's own store keyed by entry id rather than in this file.

schema_version.description: The compatibility signal for a track document, shared by every track and versioned independently of the index and the manifest. Adding an optional field keeps it. Removing a field, renaming one, changing what a field means, or adding a value to the `status` enum bumps it. Adding a category leaves it alone, since categories are data in this document rather than fixed in this schema.

generated_at.description: UTC ISO 8601 timestamp of this build, second precision, with a trailing Z.

generator_commit.description: The commit of the dfo-docs generator that produced this file. Omitted, not null, when git was unavailable at build time.

track.description: This track's id, matching the entry in roadmap.json that points here. The build checks the two agree. Entries carry no track of their own, so this field is the single authority on which tab they belong to.

categories.description: This track's filter chips, in display order. Declared rather than derived from the entries, because a chip's label is not recoverable from its id (`Aid & ODA` from `aid-oda`), because display order is a choice rather than an alphabetisation, and because a category id an entry names but this array omits fails the build instead of publishing a chip labelled with a typo. Each track declares its own vocabulary, so a data track's subjects and a platform track's subjects stay independent and neither borrows terms that mean nothing to it. Chip counts are derived by counting the entries in view that carry each id, rather than read from a count field. Chip colour is a rendering decision and is deliberately absent, so a site mapping id to colour needs a fallback for an id it has not seen. An empty array means this track renders no chip row.

entries.description: Every item in this track, upcoming and released together. This array's order carries no meaning. Split it by `status` into the upcoming and released views, then group and sort within each.

category.description: One filter chip. `id` is what entries reference and what any stored state keys on. `label` is what a reader sees, and it may be changed freely.

id.description: Stable and opaque within this track. Renaming a label leaves this alone.

entry.description: One roadmap item. An item keeps its `id` for its whole life, moving through `status` from under-consideration to released, which is what lets votes and any other stored state survive the move.

id.description: Stable and opaque, assigned once and never recomputed, and unique across every track rather than only within this one, so the site's vote store keys on the id alone. Deriving it from the title would drop that state the first time an item is renamed. Do not parse it as a slug or a route.

title.description: What the item is, as a noun phrase. Carries no version and no date, even for a released entry. The site composes those from `version` and `released_on`.

description.description: Prose, written by a person, saying what this delivers or what changed. For a released entry this is the part no pipeline can generate, which is why the whole document is authored rather than derived.

categories.description: Ids of terms in this document's `categories`. An entry may carry several, or none, in which case it appears only under the All filter.

status.description: Which view and which section the entry renders in, and the one field in this document whose value set is closed. `released` goes to the released view and the other three are the upcoming view's three sections, in the order listed here. The four values are structural, since the site lays each out differently, so a fifth value is a breaking change and bumps schema_version. Adding a category does not.

expected.description: The quarter this is expected in, sortable rather than display-formatted, so `2026-Q3` renders as `Expected: Q3 2026`. Optional on an under-consideration entry, which is by definition unscheduled. Forbidden on a released entry, which carries `released_on` instead.

released_on.description: The date this shipped, ISO 8601. Required on a released entry and forbidden on every other status. The released view's year headings come from this.

version.description: The version that shipped, without a leading v, such as `4.2.0`. Present only on a released entry, and absent where the thing released carries no version.

provenance.description: The dcid of the provenance the dataset was released under, such as `provenance/OECDCreditorReportingSystem`. Its page on Sources is `/data/sources/` followed by this dcid. Present only on a released entry, and absent where the thing released is not a dataset.

url.description: The landing page of the thing an entry describes, outside the DFO, such as a source's own data page for a dataset not yet released, so a reader can see what the entry means. A released dataset links to its page on Sources through `provenance` instead, so a consumer that finds both prefers `provenance`.
